paragraphs: Arrive sells urban mobility technology to city governments, parking operators and businesses. On the parking side that means demand insight and digital payments for parking and EV charging.

Drivers start, stop, extend and pay for a session from an app. Operators run payment stations and in-car integrations from the same platform. License plate recognition can start and end sessions automatically as cars enter and leave. The company says its EV solutions connect with more than 400 charge point operators. For city planners, dashboards report parking use, traffic trends and mobility patterns to guide planning.

Arrive describes itself as a coming together of Flowbird Group, EasyPark Group, Parkopedia and others. The about page dates the story back to 1955. That timeline opens with Cale installing its first parking meters. Within the group, Flowbird is described as delivering mobility solutions in over 6,000 cities across 80 countries. EasyPark is described as present in over 4,000 cities across more than 20 countries.

quote.text: Arrive empowers operators, decision-makers, and businesses to make smarter urban mobility choices
